metadata.title: Matrix Completion from Noisy Entries
metadata.authors: Raghunandan H. Keshavan, Andrea Montanari, Sewoong Oh

nodes.name: Noisy low-rank observation model
nodes.statement: $N = M + Z$ with $M = U\Sigma V^T$ of rank $r$; only entries $(i,j) \in E \subseteq [m]\times[n]$ are revealed, giving $N^E_{ij} = N_{ij}$ on $E$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.statement_clean: Reconstruct a rank-r matrix M from a uniformly random subset E of noisy entries N=M+Z.

nodes.name: Sampling operator $\cP_E$
nodes.statement: $\cP_E(N)_{ij} = N_{ij}$ if $(i,j) \in E$ and $0$ otherwise; maps $\reals^{m\times n}$ onto an $|E|$-dimensional subspace.

nodes.name: Average sampling rate $\eps$
nodes.statement: $\eps \equiv |E|/\sqrt{mn}$; for $m=n$ this is the average number of revealed entries per row or column.

nodes.name: $(\mu_0,\mu_1)$-incoherence
nodes.statement: $M = U\Sigma V^T$ is $(\mu_0,\mu_1)$-incoherent if (A1) $\sum_{k=1}^r U_{ik}^2 \le \mu_0 r$ and $\sum_{k=1}^r V_{ik}^2 \le \mu_0 r$ for all $i,j$, and (A2) $|\sum_{k=1}^r U_{ik}(\Sigma_k/\Sigma_1)V_{jk}| \le \mu_1 r^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Trimming
nodes.statement: Set to $0$ every row of $N^E$ with more than $2|E|/m$ revealed entries and every column with more than $2|E|/n$ revealed entries; the result is $\tN^E$.

nodes.name: Rank-$r$ projection $\T_r$
nodes.statement: If $\tN^E = \sum_i \sigma_i x_i y_i^T$ is the SVD, then $\T_r(\tN^E) = (mn/|E|) \sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i x_i y_i^T$ (rescaled best rank-$r$ approximation in Frobenius norm).

nodes.name: Cost functions $F$ and $\tF$
nodes.statement: $F(X,Y) \equiv \min_{S\in\reals^{r\times r}} \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}(N_{ij}-(XSY^T)_{ij})^2$; the regularized version $\tF(X,Y) = F(X,Y) + \rho G(X,Y)$ adds row-norm penalties $G_1(\|X^{(i)}\|^2/3\mu_0 r)$ and similarly for $Y$.

nodes.name: Grassmann manifold $\Manif(m,n)$
nodes.statement: $\tF$ is regarded as a function on $\Manif(m,n) \equiv \Grass(m,r)\times\Grass(n,r)$, the product of two Grassmann manifolds of $r$-dimensional subspaces.

nodes.name: Distance on $\Manif(m,n)$
nodes.statement: $d(\Xm_1,\Xm_2) = \sqrt{d(X_1,X_2)^2 + d(Y_1,Y_2)^2}$ where $d(X_1,X_2) = \|\theta\|_2$ for $\cos\theta_i$ the singular values of $X_1^T X_2/m$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary distances $d_-, d_+$
nodes.statement: $d_-(\Xm,\Um)^2 \equiv \Sigma_{\rm min}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + \|S-\Sigma\|_F^2$ and $d_+(\Xm,\Um)^2 \equiv \Sigma_{\rm max}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + \|S-\Sigma\|_F^2$, where $S$ minimizes $\cF(X,Y,S)$.

nodes.name: Bounded-row constraint set $\Co(\mu)$
nodes.statement: $\Co(\mu) = \{(X,Y) \in \reals^{m\times r}\times\reals^{n\times r} : \|X^{(i)}\|^2 \le \mu r,\ \|Y^{(j)}\|^2 \le \mu r\ \forall i,j\}$.

nodes.name: Independent entries noise model
nodes.statement: Entries $Z_{ij}$ are i.i.d. with $\E\{Z_{ij}\} = 0$ and sub-Gaussian tails: $\prob\{|Z_{ij}| \ge x\} \le 2 e^{-x^2/2\sigma^2}$ for some $\sigma^2$ uniformly bounded in $n$.

nodes.name: Worst case noise model
nodes.statement: $Z$ is arbitrary subject to the uniform entrywise bound $|Z_{ij}| \le Z_{\rm max}$.

nodes.name: Noisy matrix completion
nodes.statement: Given a low-rank $M$ and noisy observations $N^E$ on a uniformly random subset $E$, reconstruct $\hM$ minimizing $\|\hM - M\|_F/\sqrt{mn}$.

nodes.name: Cost minimization on Grassmann manifold
nodes.statement: Minimize the non-convex cost $\tF(X,Y)$ over $(X,Y) \in \Manif(m,n) = \Grass(m,r)\times\Grass(n,r)$ with normalization $X^TX = m\id$, $Y^TY = n\id$.

nodes.name: OptSpace
nodes.statement: Three-step matrix-completion algorithm of Keshavan-Montanari-Oh: trim, rank-$r$ project, then minimize $\tF$ by gradient descent on the Grassmann manifold $\Manif(m,n)$.
output: Estimate $\hM = X S Y^T$ of the low-rank matrix $M$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (Trim+SVD error bound)
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{mn}}\|M - \T_r(\tN^E)\|_F \le C\Mmax (nr\alpha^{3/2}/|E|)^{1/2} + C' (n\sqrt{r\alpha}/|E|)\|\tZ^E\|_2$ with probability $> 1 - 1/n^3$.
conclusions: Bound holds with probability at least $1 - 1/n^3$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 (OptSpace performance guarantee)
nodes.statement: If $|E| \ge Cn\sqrt{\alpha}\kappa^2 \max\{\mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}\log n, \mu_0^2 r^2 \alpha\kappa^4, \mu_1^2 r^2\alpha\kappa^4\}$, then with probability $\ge 1 - 1/n^3$, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{mn}}\|\hM - M\|_F \le C'\kappa^2 (n\sqrt{r\alpha}/|E|)\|Z^E\|_2$.
assumptions: $M$ is $(\mu_0,\mu_1)$-incoherent of rank $r$ and $N = M + Z$
$\hM$ is the OptSpace output on input $N^E$
RHS of the conclusion is smaller than $\Sigma_{\rm min}$
conclusions: Bound holds with probability at least $1 - 1/n^3$

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 (operator-norm bounds on $\tZ^E$)
nodes.statement: Under the independent entries model: $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le C\sigma(|E|\log n/n)^{1/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1-1/n^3$, and $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le C'\sigma(|E|/n)^{1/2}$ when $|E| \ge n\log n$. Under the worst case model: $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le 2|E|Z_{\rm max}/(n\sqrt{\alpha})$.
assumptions: $Z$ from the independent entries model (sub-Gaussian, parameter $\sigma^2$) OR the worst case model with $|Z_{ij}| \le Z_{\rm max}$
conclusions: Independent model with $|E| \ge n\log n$: $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le C'\sigma(|E|/n)^{1/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1-1/n^3$

nodes.name: Singular value perturbation of $\tN^E$
nodes.statement: $\big|\sigma_q/\eps - \Sigma_q\big| \le C\Mmax\sqrt{\alpha/\eps} + (1/\eps)\|\tZ^E\|_2$ for all $q$, with probability $> 1 - 1/n^3$ ($\Sigma_q = 0$ for $q > r$).
assumptions: Setting of Theorem 1.1: $N = M + Z$, $M$ rank $r$, $E$ uniformly random

nodes.name: Spectral-norm bound on $M - (\sqrt{mn}/\eps)\tM^E$ (KMO 2009)
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{mn}}\big\|M - (\sqrt{mn}/\eps)\tM^E\big\|_2 \le C\Mmax\sqrt{\alpha/\eps}$ with probability $> 1 - 1/n^3$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (Quadratic bounds on $F$)
nodes.section: 2.2 Auxiliary Lemmas and Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: For $\Xm \in \Manif(m,n)\cap\Co(4\mu_0)$ with $d(\Xm,\Um) \le \delta$: $F(\Xm) - F(\Um) \ge C_1 n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\,d_-(\Xm,\Um)^2 - C_1 n\sqrt{r\alpha}\|Z^E\|_2 d_+(\Xm,\Um)$ and $F(\Xm) - F(\Um) \le C_2 n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm max}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + C_2 n\sqrt{r\alpha}\|Z^E\|_2 d_+(\Xm,\Um)$, w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.
assumptions: $\eps \ge C_0 \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}\max\{\log n, \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm min}/\Sigma_{\rm max})^4\}$
conclusions: $F(\Xm) - F(\Um) \ge C_1 n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\,d_-(\Xm,\Um)^2 - C_1 n\sqrt{r\alpha}\|Z^E\|_2 d_+(\Xm,\Um)$
$F(\Xm) - F(\Um) \le C_2 n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm max}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + C_2 n\sqrt{r\alpha}\|Z^E\|_2 d_+(\Xm,\Um)$

nodes.name: Corollary 2.2 (control of $S - \Sigma$ and singular values of $S$)
nodes.section: 2.2 Auxiliary Lemmas and Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.1: $\|S - \Sigma\|_F \le C\Sigma_{\rm max} d(\Xm,\Um) + C(\sqrt{r}/\eps)\|Z^E\|_2$, $\sigma_{\rm max}(S) \le 2\Sigma_{\rm max} + C(\sqrt{r}/\eps)\|Z^E\|_2$, $\sigma_{\rm min}(S) \ge \frac{1}{2}\Sigma_{\rm min} - C(\sqrt{r}/\eps)\|Z^E\|_2$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (Gradient lower bound)
nodes.section: 2.2 Auxiliary Lemmas and Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: $\|\grad \tF(\Xm)\|^2 \ge C_1 n\eps^2 \Sigma_{\rm min}^4 [d(\Xm,\Um) - C_2 (\sqrt{r}\Sigma_{\rm max}/\eps\Sigma_{\rm min})(\|Z^E\|_2/\Sigma_{\rm min})]_+^2$ w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.
assumptions: $\eps \ge C_0 \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm max}/\Sigma_{\rm min})^2 \max\{\log n, \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm max}/\Sigma_{\rm min})^4\}$
conclusions: $\|\grad \tF(\Xm)\|^2 \ge C_1 n\eps^2 \Sigma_{\rm min}^4 [d(\Xm,\Um) - C_2(\sqrt{r}\Sigma_{\rm max}/\eps\Sigma_{\rm min})(\|Z^E\|_2/\Sigma_{\rm min})]_+^2$

nodes.name: Lemma A.1 (Quadratic bounds on $F_0$, noiseless)
nodes.statement: $C_1 \sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm min}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + C_1 \sqrt{\alpha}\|S_0 - \Sigma\|_F^2 \le \frac{1}{n\eps} F_0(\Xm) \le C_2 \sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm max}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2$, for $\Xm \in \Manif(m,n)\cap\Co(4\mu_0)$ with $d(\Xm,\Um) \le \delta$, w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.
assumptions: $\eps \ge C_0 \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}\max\{\log n, \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm min}/\Sigma_{\rm max})^4\}$
conclusions: $C_1\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm min}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2 + C_1\sqrt{\alpha}\|S_0-\Sigma\|_F^2 \le \frac{1}{n\eps}F_0(\Xm) \le C_2\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm max}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2$

nodes.name: Lemma A.2 (Gradient lower bound, noiseless)
nodes.statement: $\|\grad \tF_0(\Xm)\|^2 \ge C n\eps^2 \Sigma_{\rm min}^4 d(\Xm,\Um)^2$ for $\Xm \in \Manif(m,n)\cap\Co(4\mu_0)$ with $d(\Xm,\Um) \le \delta$, w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.
assumptions: $\eps \ge C_0 \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm max}/\Sigma_{\rm min})^2 \max\{\log n, \mu_0 r\sqrt{\alpha}(\Sigma_{\rm max}/\Sigma_{\rm min})^4\}$

nodes.name: Lemma A.3 (Directional gradient lower bound, noiseless)
nodes.statement: $\langle \grad F_0(\Xm),\Whm\rangle \ge C n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm min}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2$ for $\Xm \in \Manif(m,n)\cap\Co(4\mu_0)$ with $d(\Xm,\Um) \le \delta$, w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.
conclusions: $\langle\grad F_0(\Xm),\Whm\rangle \ge C n\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\Sigma_{\rm min}^2 d(\Xm,\Um)^2$ w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$

nodes.name: Remark 2.0 (KMO 2009): Distance-Frobenius bound
nodes.statement: If $\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_r \ge \Sigma_{\rm min}$ then $d(U,X), d(V,Y) \le (\pi/(\sqrt{2\alpha}n\Sigma_{\rm min}))\|M - \hM\|_F$.

nodes.name: Remark 2.4 (rescaling into $\Co(3\mu_0)$)
nodes.section: 2.2 Auxiliary Lemmas and Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: If $U \in \Co(\mu_0)$ and $d(X,U) \le \delta \le 1/16$, then there is $X'$ with $X'^T X' = n\id$, $X' \in \Co(3\mu_0)$, $d(X',U) \le 4\delta$, computable in $O(nr^2)$ time.

nodes.name: Nuclear-norm factor identity
nodes.origin_citation: Srebro, Rennie & Jaakkola 2005 / Recht, Fazel, Parrilo 2007

nodes.name: Candes-Plan SDP error bound
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{mn}}\|\hM_{\rm SDP} - M\|_F \le 7\sqrt{n/|E|}\|Z^E\|_F + (2/(n\sqrt{\alpha}))\|Z^E\|_F$.

nodes.name: Oracle MMSE bound
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{mn}}\|\hM_{\rm Oracle} - M\|_F \approx \sqrt{1/|E|}\|Z^E\|_F$ for the oracle estimator that knows the tangent space $T = \{UY^T + XV^T\}$.

nodes.name: Worst-case operator-norm lower bound
nodes.section: 1.8 On the Spectrum of Sparse Matrices and the Role of Trimming
nodes.statement: $\|Z^E\|_2 \ge C'(\eps) Z_{\rm max} \sqrt{\log n/\log\log n}$ under the worst case model without trimming.

nodes.name: Seginer expected operator norm bound
nodes.statement: For an i.i.d. symmetric random matrix: $\E[\|Z^E\|_2] \le C(\E[\max_i\|Z^E_{i\bullet}\|] + \E[\max_j\|Z^E_{\bullet j}\|])$.
assumptions: $Z^E$ has i.i.d. entries that are symmetric random variables

nodes.name: Talagrand concentration for Lipschitz functions on sub-Gaussian variables
nodes.statement: For a $1$-Lipschitz function $\|\cdot\|_2$ on i.i.d. zero-mean sub-Gaussian variables with parameter $\sigma^2$: $\prob(\|Z^E\|_2 - \E[\|Z^E\|_2] > t) \le \exp(-t^2/2\sigma^2)$.
assumptions: $\|\cdot\|_2$ is a $1$-Lipschitz function on $m\times n$ i.i.d. random variables $Z^E_{ij}$
$Z^E_{ij}$ have zero mean and sub-Gaussian tails with parameter $\sigma^2$

nodes.name: Rank-2 600x600 numerical experiment
nodes.statement: RMSE of OptSpace vs nuclear-norm minimization on random rank-$2$, $600\times 600$ matrices with $Z_{ij}\sim N(0,1)$, varying $|E|$ (Figure 1) and varying rank $r$ at $|E|=72000$ (Figure 2); OptSpace matches the information-theoretic lower bound after $\sim 10$ iterations.

nodes.name: Convergence of OptSpace at $|E|/n=80,160$
nodes.statement: RMSE and fit error vs iteration for $600\times 600$ rank-$2$ matrices with $\sigma=0.001$ (Figure 3); RMSE converges to the information-theoretic lower bound and fit error to $\sigma$.

nodes.name: All-ones matrix illustrating necessity of trimming
nodes.section: 1.8 On the Spectrum of Sparse Matrices and the Role of Trimming
nodes.statement: For the rank-1 all-ones $M$ with Bernoulli$(\eps/n)$ sampling, $\sigma_1(M^E) \ge \sqrt{C\log n/\log\log n}$ while $\sigma_1(\E\{M^E\}) = \eps$, so $\T_r(M^E)$ approximates $M$ poorly without trimming.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP104.1 (Singular value perturbation)
nodes.statement: Apply $\sigma_q(A+B) \le \sigma_q(A) + \sigma_1(B)$ to split $\sigma_q(\tN^E)/\eps - \Sigma_q$ into a $\tM^E$-perturbation term and a $\tZ^E$ operator-norm term; bound the first via Lemma LP104.2.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP104.1
nodes.statement: Use $\|A\|_F \le \sqrt{2r}\|A\|_2$ for rank-$\le 2r$ matrices, expand $\T_r(\tN^E)$ via SVD, apply triangle inequality, then invoke Lemmas LP104.1 and LP104.2.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP104.2
nodes.section: 2.2 Auxiliary Lemmas and Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma LP104.3 (quadratic bounds), Corollary CP104.1, and Lemma LP104.4 (gradient lower bound): show iterates stay in $\Co(4\mu_0)$, $d(\Xm_k,\Um) \le \delta/10$, then convergence to a stationary point yields the final bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP104.3 (Quadratic)
nodes.section: 2.3 Proof of Lemma Quadratic and Corollary
nodes.statement: Reduce to noiseless Lemma LP104.5 by writing $F(\Xm) = \frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(Z)\|_F^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(XSY^T-M)\|_F^2 - \langle \cP_E(Z), XSY^T-M\rangle$ and bounding the cross term using rank-$2r$ structure.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary CP104.1
nodes.section: 2.3 Proof of Lemma Quadratic and Corollary
nodes.statement: Combine the upper and lower quadratic bounds (Eqs. Quadratic1, Quadratic2) into a quadratic inequality $x^2 \le a^2 + b\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}$ in $x = \|S-\Sigma\|_F$ that yields $x \le a + b$; the singular value bounds follow by the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP104.4 (Gradient)
nodes.statement: Lower-bound $\langle \grad F(\Xm),\Whm\rangle$ by writing it as the noiseless gradient (LP104.7) minus the noise cross-term $\langle \cP_E(Z), XS\hQ^T + \hW SY^T\rangle$; bound the latter using the rank-$r$ structure of $XS\hQ^T$ and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP104.3 (independent entries)
nodes.statement: Reduce to bounding $\|Z^E\|_2$ via $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le \|Z^E\|_2$, symmetrize, apply Seginer (TP104.4) to bound $\E[\|Z^E\|_2]$, then concentrate via Talagrand (TP104.5).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP104.3 (worst case)
nodes.statement: Bound $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le Z_{\rm max}\|\tD^E\|_2$ then use trace-bounded path counting on the bipartite adjacency $\tD^E$ of degree at most $2\eps$ to conclude $\|\tD^E\|_2 \le 2\eps$.

nodes.name: Trim $N^E$
nodes.statement: Set to $0$ all rows of $N^E$ with more than $2|E|/m$ revealed entries and all columns with more than $2|E|/n$ revealed entries; output $\tN^E$.

nodes.name: Compute rank-$r$ projection
nodes.statement: Compute the SVD of $\tN^E$, retain top $r$ components, and form $\T_r(\tN^E) = (mn/|E|)\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i x_i y_i^T = X_0 S_0 Y_0^T$.

nodes.name: Gradient descent on $\Manif(m,n)$
nodes.statement: Iterate gradient descent on the regularized cost $\tF(X,Y) = F(X,Y) + \rho G(X,Y)$ over the Grassmann product manifold from $(X_0,Y_0)$ until convergence; return $\hM = X S Y^T$.

nodes.name: Apply singular-value subadditivity
nodes.statement: Use $\sigma_q(A+B) \le \sigma_q(A) + \sigma_1(B)$ with $A = \tM^E$, $B = \tZ^E$ to obtain $|\sigma_q/\eps - \Sigma_q| \le |\sigma_q(\tM^E)/\eps - \Sigma_q| + \sigma_1(\tZ^E)/\eps$.

nodes.name: Bound $\tM^E$ deviation via KMO 2009
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP104.2 to bound $|\sigma_q(\tM^E)/\eps - \Sigma_q| \le C\Mmax\sqrt{\alpha/\eps}$, and combine with the noise term to conclude.

nodes.name: Reduce Frobenius to operator norm via low rank
nodes.statement: Since $M - \T_r(\tN^E)$ has rank $\le 2r$, $\|\cdot\|_F \le \sqrt{2r}\|\cdot\|_2$.

nodes.name: Decompose into matrix-deviation, noise, and tail-SVD terms
nodes.statement: Write $M - (\sqrt{mn}/\eps)(\tN^E - \sum_{i\ge r+1}\sigma_i x_i y_i^T) = (M - (\sqrt{mn}/\eps)\tM^E) + (\sqrt{mn}/\eps)(\tZ^E - \sum_{i\ge r+1}\sigma_i x_i y_i^T)$ and apply triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Apply LP104.2 and bound tail singular value
nodes.statement: Bound the matrix-deviation term by Lemma LP104.2, the noise term by $(\sqrt{mn}/\eps)\|\tZ^E\|_2$, and use $\sigma_{r+1} \le \sigma_1(\tZ^E)$ via Lemma LP104.1.

nodes.name: Substitute $\eps = |E|/\sqrt{mn}$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Substitute the definition of $\eps$ to obtain the final bound $C'\Mmax(nr\alpha^{3/2}/|E|)^{1/2} + 2\sqrt{2}(n\sqrt{r\alpha}/|E|)\|\tZ^E\|_2$.

nodes.name: Setup and constants
nodes.statement: Set $\delta = \Sigma_{\rm min}/(C_0\Sigma_{\rm max})$ large enough so that Lemmas LP104.3 and LP104.4 apply; observe that the assumption RHS $< \Sigma_{\rm min}$ implies $(\sqrt{r}/\eps)\|Z^E\|_2 \le (\eps/C)(\Sigma_{\rm min}/\Sigma_{\rm max})^2 \Sigma_{\rm min}$.

nodes.name: Initial point bounded via TP104.1 and RP104.1
nodes.statement: Use Remark RP104.1 with Theorem TP104.1 to bound $d(\Um,\Xm_0) \le \delta/10$, using incoherence ($\Mmax \le \mu_1\sqrt{r}\Sigma_{\rm max}$).

nodes.name: Iterates remain in $\Co(4\mu_0)$
nodes.statement: Assume WLOG $\Xm_0 \in \Co(3\mu_0)$ (using rescaling Remark RP104.2); since $\tF(\Xm) \ge \rho(e^{1/9}-1)$ outside $\Co(4\mu_0)$ but $\tF(\Xm_0)$ is small, monotonicity of $\tF(\Xm_k)$ keeps iterates in $\Co(4\mu_0)$.

nodes.name: Iterates satisfy $d(\Xm_k,\Um) \le \delta/10$
nodes.statement: Combine the upper bound on $F(\Xm_0)$ and lower bound on $F(\Xm_k)$ for $d(\Xm_k,\Um) \in [\delta/10,\delta]$ to derive a contradiction with monotonicity, hence $d(\Xm_k,\Um) \le \delta/10$ for all $k$.

nodes.name: Convergence and final error bound
nodes.statement: Since $\tF$ is twice differentiable and iterates stay bounded, $\{\Xm_k\}$ converges to $\Omega = \{\Xm: d(\Xm,\Um) \le \delta, \grad\tF(\Xm) = 0\}$; Lemma LP104.4 then gives $d(\Xm,\Um) \le C(\sqrt{r}\Sigma_{\rm max}/\eps\Sigma_{\rm min})(\|Z^E\|_2/\Sigma_{\rm min})$, and Corollary CP104.1 plus Eq. (BoundDiff) yield the final bound.

nodes.name: Decompose $F(\Xm) - F(\Um)$ via $\cP_E$ identity
nodes.statement: Write $F(\Xm) = \frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(Z)\|_F^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(XSY^T - M)\|_F^2 - \langle \cP_E(Z), XSY^T - M\rangle$ and bound $F(\Um) \le \frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(Z)\|_F^2$ by setting $S = \Sigma$.

nodes.name: Apply noiseless quadratic bound
nodes.statement: Lower-bound $\frac{1}{2}\|\cP_E(XSY^T - M)\|_F^2 \ge Cn\eps\sqrt{\alpha} d_-(\Xm,\Um)^2$ via Lemma LP104.5 (noiseless quadratic).

nodes.name: Bound noise cross-term via rank-$2r$ structure
nodes.statement: Since $XSY^T - M$ has rank $\le 2r$, $|\langle \cP_E(Z), XSY^T - M\rangle| \le \sqrt{2r}\|Z^E\|_2 \|XSY^T - M\|_F$; apply triangle inequality (Eq. BoundDiff) to bound $\|XSY^T - M\|_F \le Cn\sqrt{\alpha}d_+(\Xm,\Um)$.

nodes.name: Combine for upper bound
nodes.statement: Repeat the argument with $\Xm \to \Um$ and take the difference to obtain the matching upper bound on $F(\Xm) - F(\Um)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to bounding $\|Z^E\|_2$
nodes.statement: Show $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le \|Z^E\|_2$ by trimming-zeros argument on the optimal $(x^*,y^*)$ pair, then bound $\|Z^E\|_2$ instead.

nodes.name: Apply Talagrand concentration
nodes.statement: Use that $\|\cdot\|_2$ is $1$-Lipschitz and TP104.5 to conclude $\|Z^E\|_2 \le \E[\|Z^E\|_2] + \sqrt{8\sigma^2 \log n}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - 1/n^4$.

nodes.name: Symmetrize and apply Seginer
nodes.statement: Symmetrize $Z^E_{ij}$ via independent Bernoulli signs $\xi_{ij}$ and Jensen's inequality; apply TP104.4 (Seginer 2000) to bound $\E[\|Z^E\|_2] \le C(\E[\max_i\|Z^E_{i\bullet}\|] + \E[\max_j\|Z^E_{\bullet j}\|])$.

nodes.name: Chernoff bound on column norms
nodes.statement: Apply Chernoff to $\sum_k (Z^E_{kj})^2$ with $\lambda = 3/8\sigma^2$ to obtain $\prob(\|Z^E_{\bullet j}\|^2 \ge \beta\sigma^2 \eps\sqrt{\alpha} + z) \le \exp(-(3/8)((\beta-3)\eps\sqrt{\alpha} + z/\sigma^2))$.

nodes.name: Tune $\beta$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Take $\beta = C\log n$ to bound $\E[\max_j\|Z^E_{\bullet j}\|^2] \le C\sigma^2 \eps\sqrt{\alpha}\log n$, hence $\E[\|Z^E\|_2] \le C\sigma\sqrt{\eps\sqrt{\alpha}\log n}$, giving Eq. (boundindepcase). For $|E| \ge n\log n$ use $\beta = C$ to get the tighter Eq. (boundindepcase2).

nodes.name: Reduce $\tZ^E$ to all-ones $\tD^E$
nodes.statement: Bound $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le Z_{\rm max}\|\tD^E\|_2$ since $|Z_{ij}| \le Z_{\rm max}$, where $D$ is the all-ones $m\times n$ matrix.

nodes.name: Path-counting bound on $\|\tD^E\|_2$
nodes.statement: Use $\|\tD^E\|_2^{2k} \le \Tr(((\tD^E)^T \tD^E)^k) \le n(2\eps)^{2k}$ since $\tD^E$ is the adjacency of a bipartite graph with degrees bounded by $2\eps$ after trimming.

nodes.name: Take $k$ large to conclude
nodes.statement: Letting $k \to \infty$ gives $\|\tD^E\|_2 \le 2\eps$ and hence $\|\tZ^E\|_2 \le 2\eps Z_{\rm max} = 2|E|Z_{\rm max}/(n\sqrt{\alpha})$.
